metadata.description: Get the Unicode code point of the character at a specific index, returning Nothing if out of bounds.
comments: charAt(i, s) returns Just(c) where c is the Unicode code point at position i in s, or Nothing if i is negative or i >= length(s).
Total.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.charAt.returnsCodePointAtIndex
provisions.statement: charAt returns the Unicode code point at the given zero-based index, wrapped, indexing by code point (not UTF-16 code unit), so an index after an astral (non-BMP) character is unaffected by that character's surrogate-pair width in UTF-16-based representations.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.charAt.noneWhenOutOfRange
provisions.statement: charAt returns none when the index is negative, at or beyond the string's code-point length, or when the string is empty.

parameters.name: i
parameters.description: the index of the character to retrieve

metadata.description: Concatenate a list of strings into a single string.
comments: concat(xs) returns the string formed by concatenating every string in xs in order.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's concat :: [String] -> String.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.concat.flattensPreservingOrderAndContent
provisions.statement: concat concatenates every string in the list in order, preserving all content exactly including control characters, null characters, and multi-code-point Unicode sequences (combining characters) without alteration.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.concat.emptyInputs
provisions.statement: concat of a list containing only empty strings, or of an empty list of strings, is the empty string; empty strings elsewhere in the list contribute nothing to the result.

parameters.name: xs
parameters.description: the list of strings to concatenate

comments: concat2(s, t) returns the concatenation of s and t.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's (++) :: String -> String -> String.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.concat2.appendsPreservingContent
provisions.statement: concat2 appends its second string argument to its first, preserving all content exactly including Unicode, control, and null characters.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.concat2.identityOnEmpty
provisions.statement: concat2 with either or both arguments empty returns the other argument unchanged (the empty string is the identity element).

metadata.description: Convert a list of Unicode code points to a string.
comments: fromList(cs) returns the string whose characters are the Unicode code points in cs, in order.
Code points outside the valid Unicode range [0, 0x10FFFF] yield a host-defined result (typically substitution with U+FFFD or truncation of the bits).
Total. The inverse of toList.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.fromList.buildsStringFromCodePoints
provisions.statement: fromList constructs a string whose characters are exactly the given Unicode code points, in order, including multi-code-point sequences (combining characters), control characters, and null characters.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.fromList.emptyInput
provisions.statement: fromList of an empty list of code points is the empty string.

parameters.name: cs
parameters.description: the list of Unicode code points to convert

metadata.description: Check whether a string is empty.
comments: isEmpty(s) returns true iff s is the empty string.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's null :: String -> Bool.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.isEmpty.testsZeroLength
provisions.statement: isEmpty returns true exactly when the string has no code points; any non-empty content — including whitespace, control characters, or a null character — makes it false.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: the string to test for emptiness

metadata.description: Join a list of strings with a separator between each element.
comments: join(sep, xs) returns the strings in xs concatenated with sep inserted between each pair of adjacent strings; for the empty list the result is the empty string, and for a singleton list the result is the single string.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's Data.List.intercalate :: String -> [String] -> String.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.join.insertsSeparatorBetweenStrings
provisions.statement: join concatenates a list of strings with a copy of the separator inserted between each pair of adjacent strings (not before the first or after the last), for separators of any content including empty, multi-character, and Unicode.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.join.boundaryInputs
provisions.statement: join of an empty list of strings is the empty string, regardless of separator; join of a single-element list returns that element unchanged, regardless of separator.

parameters.name: sep
parameters.description: the separator to insert between elements

parameters.name: xs
parameters.description: the list of strings to join

metadata.description: Return the length of a string.
comments: length(s) returns the number of Unicode code points in s as an int32.

Note: this is the code-point count, not the byte count or the grapheme-cluster count, so a four-byte UTF-8 character counts as one and an emoji built from multiple code points counts as the number of code points it uses.
Total on strings shorter than 2^31-1 code points.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.length.countsCodePoints
provisions.statement: length returns the number of Unicode code points in the string, not the byte count or grapheme-cluster count — so a multi-byte character counts as one code point and a combining-character sequence counts as multiple.

metadata.description: Split a string on a delimiter string.
comments: splitOn(sep, s) returns the list of substrings of s obtained by splitting on every occurrence of the non-empty delimiter sep. Adjacent or boundary delimiters produce empty-string elements in the result.
Behavior when sep is empty is host-defined and should not be relied upon.
Total. Corresponds to Haskell's Data.List.Split.splitOn :: String -> String -> [String].

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.splitOn.splitsOnEveryOccurrence
provisions.statement: splitOn splits the string into the list of substrings between every occurrence of a non-empty delimiter, including when occurrences are consecutive, overlapping, at a boundary, or span the whole string — boundary and adjacent delimiters produce empty-string elements in the result.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.splitOn.noSplitWhenAbsent
provisions.statement: splitOn returns the single-element list containing the original string when the delimiter does not occur in it.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.splitOn.emptyStringOperands
provisions.statement: splitOn on an empty string (with a non-empty separator) returns the single-element list containing the empty string; splitOn with an empty separator splits between every code point, including around an astral (non-BMP) character without breaking its surrogate-pair encoding apart.

metadata.description: Convert a string to a list of Unicode code points.
comments: toList(s) returns the list of Unicode code points making up s, in order. Each code point is represented as an int32.
Total. The inverse of fromList.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toList.decomposesIntoCodePoints
provisions.statement: toList returns the list of Unicode code points making up the string, in order, as the exact inverse of fromList, including for multi-code-point sequences and control/null characters.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toList.emptyInput
provisions.statement: toList of the empty string is the empty list.

comments: toLower(s) returns s with each character replaced by its Unicode simple (one-to-one) lowercase mapping, or itself if it has no lowercase mapping.
This is a code-point-by-code-point operation, so it does not handle the string-changing match of full Unicode case folding (e.g. U+00DF "ß" does not lowercase to "ss"; it returns itself).
For text intended for human-readable display in locales with non-trivial case mappings, prefer a host-specific full case-folding API.
Total.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toLower.appliesSimpleLowercaseMapping
provisions.statement: toLower replaces each character with its Unicode simple (one-to-one) lowercase mapping, leaving a character with no lowercase mapping unchanged — including letters, accented Unicode characters, non-letter characters (numbers, punctuation, control characters), and the empty string.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toLower.noFullCaseFoldingExpansion
provisions.statement: toLower does not perform full Unicode case folding: a character whose full lowercase mapping would expand to multiple code points (e.g. U+0130) is still mapped to its simple, single-code-point lowercase form, not the multi-code-point expansion.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: the string to convert to lowercase

comments: toUpper(s) returns s with each character replaced by its Unicode simple (one-to-one) uppercase mapping, or itself if it has no uppercase mapping.
This is a code-point-by-code-point operation, so it does not handle the string-changing match of full Unicode case folding (e.g. U+00DF "ß" does not uppercase to "SS"; it returns itself).
For text intended for human-readable display in locales with non-trivial case mappings, prefer a host-specific full case-folding API.
Total.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toUpper.appliesSimpleUppercaseMapping
provisions.statement: toUpper replaces each character with its Unicode simple (one-to-one) uppercase mapping, leaving a character with no uppercase mapping unchanged — including letters, accented Unicode characters, non-letter characters, and the empty string.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.strings.toUpper.noFullCaseFoldingExpansion
provisions.statement: toUpper does not perform full Unicode case folding: a character whose full uppercase mapping would expand to multiple code points, or whose simple mapping targets a single precomposed code point rather than a decomposed sequence, is mapped only to its simple, single-code-point uppercase form.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: the string to convert to uppercase
